samples.text: For now, the period is being run on a manual basis. The holding measure is manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period, applied by the platform team while the incident remains open. The working cause behind it is stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, and the override corrects the translation by hand rather than repairing the register entry. There is no budgeted alternative to compare against: the normal process would apply the register mapping automatically, and that path is not trusted for this period. Teams deciding whether to wait should read the override as a stopgap. It lets valuation proceed on a basis the platform team has checked, but it depends on people, not on the register, and it will need to be repeated each period until the mapping is fixed at source. Waiting for a full repair is not required to use this period's output.

The valuation failure was caused by stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. That finding is confirmed, and every other section of this review rests on it. It was not the first explanation on the table: the incident was initially recorded as overnight ERP outage, and for a short period the investigation worked on that basis. The upstream theory did not survive the evidence, because ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the outage excluded, the team examined the reference data that the inventory valuation service reads, and the stale entry was found there. Beneath the stale entry sits a weaker control, now classified as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. In plain terms, the code was wrong because nothing in the process obliged anybody to notice that it was wrong.
